related_questions.snippet: Management and Treatment Potential treatments for barotrauma are: Nasal decongestants for ear and sinus barotrauma. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy and IV fluids for pulmonary barotrauma. You may need more intensive treatment if you have severe symptoms.

related_questions.question: What is the best thing to take when you have COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: The best approach to managing COVID-19 involves a combination of symptom relief and, for those at higher risk, potentially antiviral medications, all under the guidance of a healthcare professional. Over-the-counter options like fever reducers and pain relievers (ibuprofen or acetaminophen) can help manage symptoms. If you are at higher risk of severe illness, antiviral medications such as Paxlovid or Lagevrio (molnupiravir) may be prescribed, but they need to be started within a few days of symptom onset. It's crucial to consult with a doctor to determine the most appropriate course of action for your specific situation, according to the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: fever reducers and pain relievers (ibuprofen or acetaminophen)

list.snippet: Fever and Pain: Medications like ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or acetaminophen (Tylenol) can help reduce fever and relieve aches and pains.
Cough: Cough syrups or medications can help soothe a cough.
Rest and Hydration: Getting plenty of rest and staying hydrated are also important for recovery.

list.title: Paxlovid and Lagevrio (molnupiravir):
list.snippet: These oral antiviral medications can help prevent mild COVID-19 from worsening, but they need to be started within a specific timeframe after symptom onset (usually 5-7 days).

list.title: Importance of Timely Treatment:
list.snippet: It's essential to seek medical advice and treatment promptly if you're at higher risk for severe COVID-19, as these medications are most effective when started early.

list.title: High-Risk Individuals:
list.snippet: People over 65, those with certain underlying medical conditions, and those who are immunocompromised are considered at higher risk for severe illness and should consult with a doctor promptly.

list.title: Isolation:
list.snippet: Even while taking medications, it's crucial to isolate yourself from others to prevent further spread of the virus.

list.title: Monitoring Symptoms:
list.snippet: It's helpful to track your symptoms and seek medical attention if they worsen or if you experience any concerning symptoms.

related_questions.question: What does barotrauma mean?
related_questions.snippet: Barotrauma is physical tissue damage caused by a pressure difference between an unvented space inside the body and surrounding gas or fluid. The damage is due to shear or overstretching of tissues. As a gas-filled space expands or contracts, it can cause damage to the local tissue.
